quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A hospital found that patients discharged with a follow-up appointment already scheduled had lower readmission rates than patients discharged without one. Patients who received a pre-scheduled appointment were also, on average, patients treated by physicians who had more years of experience at that hospital.
options: The pre-scheduled appointment is definitely the sole reason for lower readmissions.
Patients without pre-scheduled appointments were treated by the most experienced physicians.
Physician experience may partly explain the lower readmission rates, not the pre-scheduled appointment alone.
Readmission rates were identical regardless of appointment scheduling.
quests.correctAnswer: Physician experience may partly explain the lower readmission rates, not the pre-scheduled appointment alone.
quests.hint: Notice the detail about which physicians tended to schedule follow-up appointments before discharge.
quests.explanation: Since patients with pre-scheduled appointments were also treated by more experienced physicians, a factor that could independently affect readmission rates, the passage suggests experience may account for part of the difference.
logicChain: Patients with pre-scheduled follow-ups: lower readmission rates -> also treated by more experienced physicians -> physician experience may partly explain the difference, not scheduling alone

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's transportation office found that commuters who used carpool lanes reported shorter commute times than commuters who did not. Commuters who used carpool lanes were also required to have at least one passenger, meaning they had already coordinated their schedules with a co-worker or neighbor before leaving.
options: The carpool lane is definitely unrelated to the shorter commute times reported.
Commuters without passengers were required to use the carpool lane.
Commute times were identical regardless of lane choice.
The requirement to coordinate schedules with a passenger may relate to who chooses carpool lanes, alongside the lane's time-saving effect.
quests.correctAnswer: The requirement to coordinate schedules with a passenger may relate to who chooses carpool lanes, alongside the lane's time-saving effect.
quests.hint: Notice the requirement mentioned for using the carpool lane and what that implies about these commuters' planning.
quests.explanation: Since carpool lane use requires having a passenger and pre-coordinated schedules, the passage suggests this planning, together with the lane's typical traffic advantage, is consistent with the shorter reported commute times rather than ruling out a connection.
logicChain: Carpool lane users: shorter commute times -> lane requires a coordinated passenger -> coordination and lane access both appear consistent with the shorter commute times
